title: Social Services Legislation Amendment (Queensland Commission Income Management Regime) Bill 2017
short_title: Social Services Legislation Amendment (Queensland Commission Income Management Regime) Bill 2017

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would extend the income management arrangements linked to Queensland's Family Responsibilities Commission for a further two years in specified Cape York communities and Doomadgee.
It would replace the deadline for commission decisions of 1 July 2017 with 1 July 2019, allowing referrals made before the later date.
The extension would cover Aurukun, Coen, Hope Vale, Mossman Gorge and Doomadgee, continuing the existing arrangement for directing part of welfare payments towards priority needs.
changes: The decision cutoff in paragraph 123UF(1)(g) would move forward by two years.
The matching cutoff in paragraph 123UF(2)(h) would also move forward by two years.
Doomadgee's use of the commission referral pathway would continue for the additional period.
summary.affected: Welfare recipients subject to commission referrals in the five communities, their families and the Family Responsibilities Commission are affected.

speeches.speaker: Jenny Macklin
speeches.brief: Labor will support the Social Services Legislation Amendment (Queensland Commission Income Management Regime) Bill 2017, which extends income management in Aurukun, Coen, Hope Vale, Mossman Gorge and Doomadgee for two years, citing local community support for the measure. The speech also criticised the rushed legislative process and called for an updated independent evaluation of the Cape York welfare reform.

speeches.speaker: Paul Fletcher
speeches.brief: The bill extends the income management element of Cape York Welfare Reform for two years until 30 June 2019, covering the communities of Aurukun, Coen, Hope Vale, Mossman Gorge and Doomadgee, where 196 people are currently on income management. The extension aligns with the broader income management program's end date and was agreed with the Queensland government and the Cape York Partnership.
